title: Corrective: region-drain misalignment caused cascading fallback churn
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During an emergency regional drain initiated by a capacity vs maintenance script, the routing control-plane produced stale region affinity data for ~37 minutes. Traffic continued to be assigned to a draining region which caused capacity rejections, invoking tier-based fallback logic that cascaded through lower-cost model variants. Resulting behavior produced widespread elevated latencies and increased token unit cost due to repeated fallbacks and replays. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, and permanent fixes implemented.
timeline: 2025-01-09 02:18 UTC - Auto maintenance job triggered region-drain for eu-west-1 for urgent kernel patch (expected dry-run).
2025-01-09 02:20 UTC - Drain announcement posted to infra topic but control-plane flag did not flip due to race with cache invalidation job.
2025-01-09 02:25 UTC - Serving runtime metrics: region-affinity table still returned eu-west-1 as eligible for routing despite drain in progress; small fraction of requests routed to draining hosts.

2025-01-09 02:30 UTC - First surge of 503/CapacityRejected errors observed in downstream APIs tied to eu-west-1 pools. Automatic fallback to tier-routing triggered (prod->reserved->economy model variants).
2025-01-09 02:31 UTC - Fallback loop began: clients retried with same session rules; routing policy attempted to select next preferred region but used stale region rankings from the policy cache.
2025-01-09 02:45 UTC - Control-plane engineer Priya Singh alerted on PagerDuty; mitigation started.
2025-01-09 02:53 UTC - Emergency kill-switch: disable autoscale-provisioner temporarily and force policy cache invalidation; routing stabilized over next 10 minutes.
2025-01-09 03:05 UTC - Full recovery: error rates normalized, latency returned to baseline. Post-incident monitoring continued for 24h.
2025-01-09 10:12 UTC - Initial postmortem draft created and triage review scheduled.
2025-01-13 16:00 UTC - Engineering postmortem review with oncall, runtime, and control-plane teams. Action items assigned to implement permanent fixes.
detection: Automated SLO alerts flagged a 2x tail latency increase and a rise in 503 CapacityRejected for requests originating from EU region; alert correlated to region-drain event recorded by infra but control-plane flagged mismatch. PagerDuty triggered from the routing SLO runbook.
impact_summary: Approximately 12% of requests during the incident window experienced degraded success (increased latency or transient errors). Several customers using dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 observed degraded throughput. Token billing increased by ~21% for impacted workloads due to repeated fallbacks and auto-retries.
root_cause: Concurrent operations caused a race between the region-drain orchestration (infra) and the routing policy cache invalidation (control-plane). The drain workflow updated the authoritative region state but did not wait for the control-plane to acknowledge and invalidate in-memory affinity caches. Routing policy used stale region eligibility and attempted tiered fallbacks; retry semantics on clients and lack of idempotent session hints caused cascading fallback churn.
immediate_mitigation: Forced cache invalidation across control-plane routing agents (propagate flush message) to remove eu-west-1 from eligible region lists.
Temporarily disabled automatic client-side retry for breadth-first fallbacks for 30 minutes to prevent replay amplification.
Put an emergency guard in autoscaler to prevent simultaneous pool drain + capacity reduction operations in the same maintenance window.
permanent_fixes: Implement two-phase drain handshake: infra drain request must receive explicit ACK from control-plane before traffic is moved. The handshake includes a generation token to ensure cache coherence.
Add CAS (compare-and-swap) semantics to routing policy cache updates so older state updates cannot overwrite newer drain signals.

Introduce a short-term grace window where clients will prefer regional failover instead of model-variant fallback when region drain is detected to reduce repeated model swaps and associated token cost.
Enhance fallback logic to consider recent fallback-count per session (circuit-breaker) to prevent cascading churn; add a fallback backoff multiplier to throttled clients.
Update runbook: add explicit check-step to verify cache invalidation ACK when performing incipient region operations.
tests_and_validation: End-to-end staging test added that simulates drain handshake and verifies no request routing during the handshake period.
Chaos test introduced to the continuous routing test-suite that triggers concurrent drain+cache updates to validate CAS behavior.
Load test showing fallback-circuit reduces repeated fallback occurrences by 92% under similar workload patterns.
followups: ENG-8333 - rollout two-phase drain handshake and monitor for false positives (owner: Jacob Nguyen).
ENG-8340 - client-sdk change: add retry-idempotency hint and expose 'prefer-region-failover' flag (owner: Maya Chen).
PM-410 - communicate incident summary and cost impact to top-10 customers impacted and offer credits (owner: Priya Singh).
DES-210 - update console UX to surface active region-drain handshakes in routing dashboard (owner: Omar Khatri).
notes: We observed that most client retries were immediately retried without jitter which amplified load on fallback regions; recommend SDK defaults include exponential jitter.

Edge case: if a drain is triggered as part of an automated upgrade and capacity is already low, the old policy allowed immediate reassignment to draining hosts if the cache hadn't been invalidated yet. This sequence is now guarded by the handshake.
Cost analysis attached: snapshot from billing dashboard (link below) shows token billing spike during incident window.
